title: Home systems: routines, shared chores, meals and money

say: Home systems: routines, shared chores, meals and money.
This is the video for Module 3, Home Management Systems.
A routine is a set of tasks done in the same order at roughly the same time. Routines save time because you stop deciding what to do next.

panel.heading: A home that runs without you holding it all
items: Routines save you deciding what comes next

say: They also make it easier for others in the home to help, because everyone knows what happens when.

say: Most of a calm morning is actually prepared the night before. That is why the best first routine is the evening reset.

say: Even 20 to 30 minutes each evening makes a big difference. Clear the kitchen and wash the pots. Set out uniforms and bags.

panel.heading: The evening reset
items: Kitchen cleared and pots washed
Uniforms and bags ready
Quick check of tomorrow's plan
Phones charging
10-minute tidy with everyone helping

say: Check tomorrow's plan, put the phones on charge, and do a 10-minute tidy of the main room with everyone helping.
Then spread the big cleaning across the week, one main task a day of 20 to 40 minutes, so Saturday is lighter.

say: When you clean bathrooms and toilets, never mix bleach, such as Hypo, with other cleaning products. Dangerous gases can form.
Open windows, wear gloves, and store all chemicals high up, in their labelled containers, away from children and food.

say: If one woman carries most of the work, working faster will not fix it. Sharing will.
First, list every task the home needs. Include the mental load, like remembering fees deadlines or noticing the gas is low.

panel.heading: Share chores in three steps
items: List every task, including the mental load
Match tasks to age and ability
Agree at a 20-minute family meeting
Post a chore chart and review monthly

say: Second, match tasks to ability. Children can do more than we expect, but keep young children away from hot pots, knives, chemicals and sockets.

panel.heading: Share chores in three steps
items: List every task, including the mental load
Match tasks to age and ability
Agree at a 20-minute family meeting
Post a chore chart and review monthly

say: Third, hold a short family meeting. Let each person choose some tasks first, then post the chart.

For example, Fatima in Ilorin listed 28 tasks. Her son chose dishes and sweeping, her daughter chose setting the table, and her husband took the Saturday market run. Her housework dropped by about 1.5 hours a day.

say: A common mistake is handing over only the doing. Please buy gas when I tell you still leaves the remembering with you. And redoing their work teaches them it does not matter.

panel.heading: Hand over the whole task
left: Please buy gas when I tell you
right: You are in charge of buying gas
Accept good enough, and say thank you

say: Instead, hand over the whole task. You are in charge of buying gas: check the level every Friday and buy when it is low. Accept good enough, and thank them specifically.

say: Plan the week's meals from what you already have, write one market list, and cook a big pot of stew that serves several meals. Then keep it safe.
Wash your hands, and use separate boards for raw meat and ready-to-eat food.

cards.d: Wash hands before cooking and after raw meat or fish. Keep raw and cooked food apart.
Into the fridge or freezer within 2 hours, in covered one-meal portions. Never leave stew out overnight.
Reheat until steaming hot all the way through, and only once.

say: Cool cooked food quickly and put it in the fridge or freezer within 2 hours, in covered portions for one meal. Do not leave stew out overnight.

Reheat until steaming hot all the way through, and only once.

say: Reheat until steaming hot all the way through, and reheat only once. If frozen food fully thaws in a long power cut, cook it straight away or throw it away.

say: A budget is a plan for your money before you spend it. Split it into needs, wants and savings.
For example, Ruth and her husband in Jos bring in about 400,000 naira a month.
Needs like rent, food, school fees, transport and gas come to 320,000 naira. That is 80%, and in many Nigerian households needs take more than half. That is fine.
They save 40,000 naira, which is 10%, and keep 40,000 for wants.
Together that is 400,000. Every naira has a job.
Meal planning cut their food spending from about 160,000 to 140,000, and the 20,000 saved goes to the emergency fund. Never share your PIN or OTP with anyone.

To remember. Start with the evening reset. Share whole tasks, not just the doing. Keep batch-cooked food safe. Give every naira a job. And keep one family calendar, starting checklists four to six weeks before busy times like school resumption.

panel.heading: Remember

One family calendar: if it is not on it, it is not planned
